question.text: If the pressure, temperature and density of an ideal gas are denoted by $p, T$ and $\rho$, respectively, the velocity of sound in the gas is

solution.text:
$v=\sqrt{\frac{\gamma R T}{M}}=\sqrt{\frac{\gamma P}{\rho}}$
(i) Velocity of sound is proportional to $\sqrt{T}$
$\therefore$
$v \propto \sqrt{T}$
(ii) When $\rho$ is constant, the velocity of sound is proportional to root of pressure $P$
$\therefore$
$$
v \propto \sqrt{P}
$$
